name: Purple amethyst cluster 900
prompt: a rough natural boulder outcrop breaking out of the ground with smooth glassy blue-white soulstone veins running through the rock, the stone mass dominant, not a freestanding crystal cluster and not a carved slab, purple amethyst cluster, about as tall as an adult person, self-emissive at night, softly radiating light: deep violet heart-light pulsing slowly

placement.note: ONE SCENERY PIXEL IS ONE PLAYER PIXEL. world_px_height IS the art's own alpha bbox height, so scenery is placed into the world at 1:1 exactly as the avatar is (setScale(1)) and the two share one pixel grid. The CAMERA still zooms the whole scene — that is uniform and correct; what must never happen is scenery being resampled on its own, against the player. world_height_m is what the art reads as beside a 87px character; declared_height_m is what it was once declared to be, and a gap between them means the ART is the wrong size.

adopted: recovered from the PixelLab store 2026-08-13: runs 5/6 were cancelled mid-pass and their committed-but-unpushed art died with the runners; the store object survived. Index 900+ band avoids colliding with the concurrently-running pass.
recovered_spec: metadata restored by replaying run 5's deterministic planner at its checkout (a21c4bc8); orphan creation order matched the planned sequence exactly

motion.description: This is the same picture in every frame. ONLY the bright veins across the rock brighten a little and return. Everything else in the picture is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel, unchanged in shape, size, position and colour. No outline anywhere is redrawn. The last frame matches the first frame exactly, so the loop joins. Nothing anywhere becomes darker, lighter or a different colour except the one thing named above.

This is the same picture in every frame. ONLY the glowing veins across the rock brighten a little and return. It is lit and clearly visible in every frame, including the first. It gets only SLIGHTLY brighter -- never white, never washed out -- and keeps its own colour throughout: brightest in the middle, back to its first-frame brightness at the end, never dimmer at the end than the start. Nothing is added or removed anywhere: every object appears in every frame, the same number of them, in the same places, at the same size. Everything else is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel: same shape, size, position and colour, no outline redrawn. The last frame matches the first exactly.

This is the same picture in every frame. ONLY the white vein across the rock brightens a little and returns. It is lit and clearly visible in every frame, including the first. It gets only SLIGHTLY brighter -- never white, never washed out -- and keeps its own colour throughout: brightest in the middle, back to its first-frame brightness at the end. It stays exactly the same size and shape in every frame: it never grows and never spreads, only its brightness shifts. Every object stays the same kind of thing it is in the first frame and keeps its own colour: nothing turns into anything else. Nothing is added or removed anywhere: every object appears in every frame, the same number of them, in the same places, at the same size. Everything else is copied from the first frame exactly, pixel for pixel: same shape, size, position and colour, no outline redrawn. The last frame matches the first exactly.
